doc.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Charlie Watts, the Rolling Stones and 'The In Crowd'
summary: Ingham recalls Charlie Watts sitting in at a London club and talks with Rowe about Ramsey Lewis and Bohemian Caverns.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I know they are. Isn’t that sad? Geriatric rockers? Exactly. They’re older than we are. They’re getting ready for another tour, just to make another zillion millions. Charlie Watts, the drummer with them, I knew him in London. He used to come in and sit in with the band where we played, in the Cafe Des Artiste in the Fulham Road. He was dreadful, but he did love jazz. Charlie’s always loved jazz. I think he played once.
Yeah, he did a big band.

Yeah, he loves jazz. He also likes picking up the Charlie Parker thing, and I know he loved Earl Hines and things. I mean God knows he must have felt a fish out of water with those other guys. I don’t think Jagger liked jazz at all. I think the only record he ever liked was Ramsey Lewis’ “The In Crowd.” Do you remember that?
[scats]. Well it had a great beat to it.
The piano was out of tune, too.
Oh wonderful, oh done in that Bohemian Caverns.
It’s got that kind of thing you were talking about.
Exactly. That’s the atmosphere. Exactly. Can you imagine the bodies and all the sweat when they were done.
